resolutions: Intake creates .factory/stories/<KEY>/ (operator 2026-08-18): story_uses_scoped_layout already keys on that directory, so intake mkdir-ing it IS the activation - new story goes story-scoped/untracked-pointer/ship-in-place, legacy (dir absent) stays legacy. No new marker format.

Trust audit + full-suite gate (operator 2026-08-18): the grep enumerated the hand-joined .factory/history and grills/plan reads (plans.py, check_board_complete, findings, audit); the merge-simulation + shipped-visible required tests and the full suite fail loudly on a missed consumer - a miss is a gate failure, not a silent break.

Split into sequential stages that ship together (operator 2026-08-18): on a budget-overrun signal, re-decompose into consumer-migration then intake-activation + merge-sim gate, both in this worktree landing in the same PR (0046 atomic ship). Otherwise one delegation.

Migrate the 32 stale tests (all now required tests; test_gates.py in scope) - the tests encode the old layout, production is correct, so FIX THE TESTS not the behavior. Pattern A (mechanical, ~25): a shipped story's evidence is at .factory/stories/<KEY>/ not .factory/history/<KEY>/ (ship-in-place); singleton evidence -> story-dir; run.json legacy assertions -> derived phase / untracked-pointer reality. Pattern B (~7, e.g. test_pr_ready_legacy_story_still_archives_to_history, test_stage_migrate_*, intake_after_ship, intake_preserves_signoff): these verify LEGACY behavior but intake now always creates the marker - construct a marker-ABSENT story (remove .factory/stories/<KEY> after intake, or place legacy artifacts manually) so the legacy path is still exercised; do NOT weaken the legacy code. Make each of the 35 required tests pass; the orchestrator runs the full suite to catch stragglers.
